The Content-Security-Policy contains directives such as 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval', wildcard sources or plain http: sources in script-related directives, significantly reducing its effectiveness against XSS.

findings.remediation: Remove 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' from script-src/default-src, replace wildcards with explicit origins and use nonce- or hash-based allowlisting with 'strict-dynamic'.

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy header missing
findings.description: The HTML response does not define a Content-Security-Policy. Without CSP the browser has no policy to restrict script sources, which removes an important mitigation against cross-site scripting and data injection.

findings.title: Sensitive response cacheable (missing Cache-Control: no-store)
findings.description:
A response that sets session cookies or contains a login form does not prevent caching. Shared proxies or browser history on shared machines may retain sensitive content.

Response considered sensitive because it sets session cookie(s): PORTALSESSID and contains a password input.
findings.remediation: Send 'Cache-Control: no-store' (and 'Pragma: no-cache' for HTTP/1.0 caches) on authenticated and credential-handling responses.

findings.title: Cookie scoped to parent domain
findings.description:
A cookie's Domain attribute is set to a parent domain, so it will be sent to every sibling subdomain. A compromise of any less-secure subdomain exposes or allows overwriting of this cookie.

Cookie 'PORTALSESSID' is sent to every host under 'acme-corp.example', not only 'app.acme-corp.example'.
findings.remediation: Omit the Domain attribute (host-only cookie) or use the __Host- prefix so the cookie is only sent to the issuing host.
findings.cwe_name: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere

findings.title: Cookie without SameSite attribute

findings.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

findings.title: Password field with autocomplete enabled
findings.description: A password input does not set an autocomplete hint. Browsers may store the value; on shared workstations this can expose credentials. Modern guidance permits password managers, so treat as informational.
findings.remediation: Use autocomplete="current-password" / "new-password" to cooperate with password managers, or autocomplete="off" for high-risk shared-terminal contexts.

findings.title: Permissions-Policy header missing
findings.description: No Permissions-Policy is defined, so powerful browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation, payment) are not explicitly restricted for this origin and embedded frames.
findings.remediation: Send a Permissions-Policy disabling unused features, e.g. 'Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=()'.

findings.title: Referrer-Policy header missing
findings.description: No Referrer-Policy is defined. Modern browsers default to strict-origin-when-cross-origin, but older clients may leak full URLs (including tokens in query strings) to third parties.
findings.remediation: Send 'Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin' or 'no-referrer' for sensitive applications.
findings.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

findings.title: security.txt not published
findings.description: No RFC 9116 security.txt file was found at /.well-known/security.txt, so researchers have no documented channel to report vulnerabilities.
findings.remediation: Publish /.well-known/security.txt with at least Contact and Expires fields, ideally signed and including a Policy link.

retest_queue.title: State-changing form without anti-CSRF token
retest_queue.description:
A POST form does not contain a hidden field matching common anti-CSRF token names. Unless protected by SameSite cookies or custom headers, it may be vulnerable to cross-site request forgery. Requires manual confirmation.

1 POST form(s) without a recognizable anti-CSRF hidden field.
retest_queue.remediation: Add a per-session or per-request synchronizer token to all state-changing forms and validate it server-side; also set SameSite on session cookies.
